stemBlocks.value: The marks out of 10 gained by 40 students on an essay writing test are: mark 4 (3 students), 6 (9), 7 (8), 8 (7), 9 (8), 10 (5). (i) Calculate the students' mean score. (ii) Determine (a) the modal mark and (b) the median mark.
Think first: With a frequency table the mean needs Σfx, not the sum of the six different marks.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p224-q10 from workbook page 224.

solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply each mark by its frequency and add.
Divide by the total number of students.
Pick out the mark with the highest frequency.
Build a running total to find the 20th and 21st marks.

contentBlocks.value: Cumulative: 3, 12, 20, 27, 35, 40 — so the 20th student scored 7 and the 21st scored 8

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply each mark by its frequency and divide the total by 40 for the mean, take the mark with the largest frequency for the mode, and use a running total to locate the 20th and 21st marks for the median.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) Mean = 300 ÷ 40 = 7.5 marks  (ii)(a) Modal mark = 6  (b) Median mark = 7.5

whyThisWorks.value: A frequency table is a compressed list: the mark 6 appearing nine times contributes 6 × 9 to the total, which is why the mean is Σfx ÷ Σf. The mode is about how often a mark occurs, so it is the mark beside the largest frequency — not the largest frequency itself. The median is a position, and cumulative totals tell you which mark the 20th and 21st students in order actually scored.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing Σfx by 6 (the number of different marks) instead of by 40.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing Σfx by 6 (the number of different marks) instead of by 40.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving the mode as 9, the frequency, rather than 6, the mark.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Giving the mode as 9, the frequency, rather than 6, the mark.

commonErrors.misconception: Taking the median as the middle row of the table instead of the middle student.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting that with 40 students the median averages the 20th and 21st values.
